title: Gigli with Courgette
subtitle: Ruffled lily-shaped pasta with courgette and lemon
excerpt: Gigli are frilly cone-shaped pasta from Tuscany. Courgette ribbons coat the ruffles with a light lemon and olive oil sauce. It is bright, quick, and needs no tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Tuscan approach to pairing gigli pasta with summer vegetables, adapted into a simple lemon and courgette preparation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This is best made and eaten straight away. The courgette wilts if kept.

content.text: Gigli hold light sauces inside their ruffled cones. Slice the courgette into thin ribbons so it cooks quickly without turning mushy. Use the pasta water to build the sauce into something silky.

items.prepNote: sliced into thin ribbons with a peeler

content.text: Cook the pasta in a large pan of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a large mugful of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the courgette ribbons and a pinch of salt. Toss and cook for 3 minutes until just tender but not soft.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with 4 tablespoons of pasta water. Toss well over a low heat.
Add the lemon zest and juice. Add half the parmesan. Toss again, adding more pasta water if needed.
Serve straight away with the remaining parmesan and fresh basil.

items.cause: It cooked too long or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Use high heat and cook for 3 minutes only. It should keep a slight bite.

items.symptom: The sauce looks oily rather than creamy.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added.
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time and toss briskly to emulsify.
Add more lemon juice and check the pasta water was well salted.
